checks: The hull over endpoints zero and one has exactly the prescribed two integer fibers. The same is true after independent small vertex changes, since a convex combination at an endpoint uses only that endpoint.

The thresholds at z=0 are (1/3,1/3,-1), and at z=1 they are (-1,-1,1/3). A threshold -1 is strict full on its reference triangle. The sums -1/3 and -5/3 are less than one, so no point of either whole affine plane can strictly violate all three margins.

The accepted positive modes give all zero-sum row vectors. The first fiber independently contributes the first two coordinates and the second fiber contributes any third coordinate. Full traces have derivative zero on these trace-zero modes. The three derivatives therefore span the entire three-dimensional codomain.
The source locator is the partial-tuple example in §6. Equal budgets at the displayed reference masses make all three constraints active and the argument needs no critical-depth premise.

dependencies.verification: Specialize to d=2, m=3 and the fixed canonical centroid halfspaces on each physical endpoint simplex. The row multiplier is -6/5 on the zero-sum c space. Strict full traces use ordinary volume differentiation.

overlap.comparison: Supplies the positive velocity space and proper-trace derivative for each individual triangle. It does not give the two-fiber rank counterexample.
Its one shared complete tuple has all canonical traces in every varied copy. The current first derivative is restricted to the positive spaces and uses only a partial proper tuple in each fiber.

readability: The notation λ_i denotes the same ambient affine barycentric function at both reference fibers, while each nearby vertex chart varies the simplex against those fixed margins.
review_method: Independent cold reading of the frozen proof, then direct checks of the archived source locators, pinned predecessors and mathematical arguments.
